title: Actual Patient Pay After Approval: Notice Amounts, Partial Months and Reconciliation of Estimates
content:
## Clauses in force

Under Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage, once eligibility is approved, each eligible month is billed the patient pay amount on the County Assistance Office notice in effect for that month, with charge basis "actual (notice)"; a redetermined amount, including the January change from the Social Security cost-of-living increase, applies from the first day of the month the notice names. Patient pay is unchanged for a month with Medicaid reserved bed days. Within the trueup days after the approval notice, every month billed as an estimate is reconciled: where the actual patient pay exceeds the estimates billed for the month, the difference is billed with charge basis "true-up increase". Estimates billed for months before the eligibility start date are reduced with reason "not-eligible month", because those months are private-pay months. For the hospice tier, patient pay collected is credited against the hospice's room-and-board payment. The Medicaid payment plus patient pay is payment in full: a Medicaid resident is never charged for items or services the Medicaid per diem covers. A charge is reduced once per adjustment reason — the system's billing record for the charge shows which reasons have already been used on it.

## Clauses no longer in force, with their current wording

1. "Patient pay never exceeds the month's cost of care", read with the month's cost of care always as the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, is no longer in force in that unqualified form. Current wording: patient pay never exceeds the month's cost of care. For an actual-billed month that the actual-month review prices, a reconciled estimate month that the estimate reconciliation prices and a pending estimate month that the pending-month review prices, the month's cost of care is the cost of care that review's own pricing gives, and only for such a month; every other month remains under the base rule, where the month's cost of care is the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate.
2. "Where it is lower, the estimate is reduced by the difference with reason true-up decrease", as an unqualified clause, is no longer in force. Current wording: where the actual patient pay of the month is lower than the estimates billed for it, the estimate is reduced by the difference with reason "true-up decrease", the actual patient pay of a reconciled estimate month being the lesser of the patient pay the notice sets for that month and the month's cost of care; this holds for the latest month billed as an estimate, by service month, on a case whose eligibility has been approved, and only for such a month; every other reconciliation remains under the base rule, where a lower actual patient pay reduces the estimate by the difference with reason "true-up decrease".
3. "In a month of admission, discharge or death, patient pay is the lesser of the monthly patient pay and the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, with charge basis partial month, and any amount already billed above that is reduced with reason cost-of-care cap", as an unqualified clause, is no longer in force. Current wording: for a reconciled estimate month that the estimate reconciliation prices and a pending estimate month that the pending-month review prices, a month of admission, discharge or death takes the cost of care that review's own pricing gives in place of the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, and only for such a month; every other month of admission, discharge or death remains under the base rule, by which patient pay is the lesser of the monthly patient pay and the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, with charge basis "partial month", and any amount already billed above that is reduced with reason "cost-of-care cap".

## Reading the clauses

*A notice issued in one month names a later month as effective.* The redetermined amount applies from the first day of the month the notice names.

*A month has Medicaid reserved bed days.* Patient pay for that month is unchanged.

*An estimate was billed for a month before the eligibility start date.* That month is a private-pay month; the estimate is reduced with reason "not-eligible month".
